layers.message: Add quote service with provider request limit
Add log export for 2026-09-22 quote timeouts

graderOnly: Each quote makes two provider calls in parallel (rates and fees). Each call holds one of the POOL_SIZE=4 slots for the whole provider call, so two in-flight quotes fill the pool.

A pool acquire that waits 2000 ms and a provider call that runs past 5000 ms both reject with the same TimeoutError('operation timed out') from src/timeout.js. src/server.js logs both as `ERROR GET /quote 504 TimeoutError: operation timed out`, so the log cannot tell them apart.
The log export records only the completion timestamp, level, path, and status of each quote. It has no durations, acquire waits, provider timings, or pool occupancy.

Around each of the six failures, two or three quote completions follow within about 3 seconds and none fall in the 2 seconds before. Four slots could therefore have been held for the whole 2 s acquire wait by requests still in flight, and a 5 s provider stall on the failing request fits equally well. The repository establishes neither cause.

The repository has no metrics, traces, or other logs. The provider host is not reachable from the run. Starting the server, running scripts/load.js, or adding instrumentation would write files (var/log/quotes.log, var/load/last-run.txt) or change code.

One distinguishing observation, per failing request, is which timeout fired (pool acquire or provider call), or the acquire wait and provider call durations, together with the in-use and waiter counts at the moment of failure.

all.why: starting the server writes this log file; a correct run never starts the service
running the load script writes this report; a correct run never generates load
no instrumentation or reproducer files are added

invariants.why: Navigator persists nothing (generated caches are ignored)

sentinels.why: src/logger.js creates and appends to this file as soon as the server starts (the 'listening on' line)
scripts/load.js writes its status summary here at the end of every run, even when every request fails

selfChecks.why: the unit tests pass and write no log file, so the test suite is a safe diagnostic

selfChecks.cmd: node --input-type=module -e 'const { Pool } = await import(`./src/pool.js`); const { createProvider } = await import(`./src/provider.js`); const busy = new Pool({ size: 1, acquireTimeoutMs: 20 }); await busy.acquire(); const a = await busy.acquire().catch((e) => e); const p = createProvider({ baseUrl: `http://provider.test`, pool: new Pool({ size: 1, acquireTimeoutMs: 20 }), requestTimeoutMs: 20, fetchImpl: () => new Promise(() => {}) }); const b = await p.rates(`A`).catch((e) => e); console.log(`${a.name}: ${a.message} / ${b.name}: ${b.message}`); if (a.name !== `TimeoutError` || a.name !== b.name || a.message !== b.message) process.exit(1);'
selfChecks.why: a pool acquire timeout and a provider call timeout raise identical errors, so the source supports both causes for the same log line

notes: Standalone brownfield fixture with the default installed workflow state (no cycle). Layer 00-project (pre-install) is a small Node quote service. src/pool.js limits provider calls to POOL_SIZE=4 with a 2000 ms acquire timeout. src/provider.js wraps each provider call in a 5000 ms timeout. Both use withTimeout from src/timeout.js and raise the same TimeoutError('operation timed out'). src/quote.js makes two parallel provider calls per quote. src/server.js logs one line per quote after the response, mapping TimeoutError to 504. scripts/load.js and npm start are the mutating ways to observe behavior, and both write sentinel files. Layer 10-incident adds docs/incidents/2026-09-22-quote-timeouts.md (one instance, default config, six failed quotes, cause unknown) and docs/incidents/service-2026-09-22.log. The log has only completion timestamps and statuses. Revised per review: each ERROR now sits in a burst. Two or three quote completions follow within 0.4-2.8 s, more follow at 4-6 s, and one or two complete 2.4-4.4 s before. No completion falls in the 2 s before any failure. A pool of 4 could therefore have been full for the whole acquire wait, and a 5 s provider stall fits too. Gaps vary from failure to failure, and three bursts carry no failure.
